sentences.text:
Sections 4/6 Of The Pocso Act vs Allowed In Re : Sagnik Sen
@Joy on 15 April, 2024
tkm/ct 28 C.R.M. (DB) 1135 of 2024
sl no. 37

In Re : An application for bail under section 439 of   Procedure in connection with Chandannagore P.S case n  2023 dated 12.12.2023 under sections 417/376(2)(i)(n)
sections 4/6 of the POCSO Act  and  Allowed In Re : Sagnik Sen @Joy   Mr. Bitasok Banerjee  Mr. A Salam  ...... for th  Mr. Sudip Kumar  Mr. Samarjit Balial  ...... for th  1.
Petitioner is in custody for 122 days.
He submits there was a romantic relationship between him and the victim.
He prays for bail.
2. Learned lawyer for the State opposes the bail prayer.
3. We have considered the materials on record.
We have also noted the statement of the victim.
She stated she had a physical relationship with the petitioner.
She also had a physical relationship with his friend namely Argha Choudhury.
Strangely the said Argha Choudhury has not been arrayed as an accused in the case.
4. Under such circumstances we are of the opinion petitioner may be released on bail.

5. Accordingly, the petitioner be released on bail upon furnishing a bond of Rs. 10,000/- with two sureties of like amount each, one of whom must be local to the satisfaction of the learned ACJM Chandannagore on condition that the petitioner shall appear before the trial court on every date of hearing and shall not Signed By :
TAMAL KRISHNA MANDAL High Court of Calcutta 18 th of April 2024 04:27:19 PM intimidate witnesses or tamper with evidence in any manner whatsoever.
6. In the event he fails to appear before the trial court without justifiable cause, the trial court shall be at liberty to cancel his bail automatically without reference to this court.
